title: Composite dark-baryon dark matter with a 300 keV hyperfine splitting: a UV origin for the LZ event?
question: Can a composite DM state (dark baryon/atom/heavy-light hadron) naturally have a spin-flip partner split by delta = 250-400 keV at 0.3-4 TeV, which mediators give the LZ transition rate, and what follows for the excited-state lifetime, self-interactions and relic abundance?
headline_result: A heavy-light dark hadron (m_Q ~ 1 TeV, Lambda_D = 0.42 GeV) gives delta = 300 keV as the B*-B splitting scaled by m_b/m_Q; hyperfine partners couple only via spin-dependent (M1 or axial) operators; the photon-M1 moment for one LZ event, 2.1e-4 mu_N, implies tau(chi2 -> chi1 gamma) = 66 us and a single-site ceiling delta <= 326 keV (excluding P007's 358-380 keV window for photon-M1 models); a G_F-strength axial Z spin flip gives 0.64 events at 300 keV
key_numbers: Coulombic alpha_eff = 0.0366 at 1 TeV/300 keV (SU(3)_D Lambda_D = 8.5 eV; thermal alpha -> 3.7 keV); heavy-light Lambda_D = 0.42/0.63 GeV (meson/Sigma_Q-like), 184 keV at Lambda_QCD; light baryon suppression 9.6e-7; mu_tr(N=1) = 2.11e-4 mu_N = 2.2e-18 e cm = 0.225 e/(2m) at 300 keV, 3.40e-3 mu_N at 366; A' suppression 0.122/2.2e-3/3.0e-5 at 0.3/1/3 GeV; eps(heavy-light, alpha_D=0.1) = 2.6e-5 (massless)/5.5e-4 (1 GeV); eps(dark atom) = 0.05; Z-axial N = 0.64 (300), 0.0027 (366), N=1 at 290 keV; tau = 66 us / 0.14 us; tau >= 12.7 us -> delta <= 326 (306-350) keV; eta_D = 4.4e-13; sigma/m = 3e-8/1.6e-5/2.5e-11 cm^2/g; glueball 2.3 GeV; elastic normalisation vs P012 0.4%
model_or_mechanism: composite hyperfine inelastic DM: Coulombic dark atom, HQET heavy-light dark hadron, light-constituent dark baryon; photon/dark-photon M1 transition (P012 NREFT coefficients with A' propagator), Z-axial O4 inelastic; Gamma = mu^2 delta^3/pi lifetime; asymmetric relic
